title: I Tried Creating a Game Using Real-World Geographic Data
beats: Rainy afternoon, old unfinished pilot-delivery game, Sudan-shaped hole bug; decides to restart from scratch
Cube to sphere by normalizing; result is broken until a typo (minus for plus) is fixed; then notes corner clumping and swaps in a fancier equation
Heightmap origin (shuttle radar, ship sonar) and the lat/long conversion functions, tested by wrapping and unfurling animation
Projects heightmap onto sphere, vertices pushed out; tangent into plate tectonics curiosity
Shader colours land above sea level, then sea level is lowered slider-style so islands join and depth becomes visible
Player controller; poles break the camera; fixed by fiddling; South Pole hole joke
Frustum culling defined; 6 chunks cull poorly, so split faces into sub-faces; reduce vertices; GPU gets happier
Normal vector defined; compute shader samples 4 neighbours, cross product gives per-pixel normal; side-by-side old vs new
Country outlines as point lists; inefficient compute shader loops all countries and segments per pixel; admits better way unknown
Convoluted plan to highlight visited country: write index per pixel (point-in-polygon found online), visit-time buffer, shader brightens recent
Ocean depth blend, specular, scrolling normal maps, triplanar mapping pointer to old video
Distance field by vertical then horizontal iterative passes for foam; slow; mentions jump flooding for later
Boats; wake via blur fails; custom trail renderer eats an afternoon; concludes builtin would have worked
Clouds from instanced spheres, spawn by best-of-random-candidates noise; first try wrong, tune noise scale to 10; blur, normals, inverted bug
Hand-rolled shadows: draw from light's view and transform; upside-down shadows; fix from obscure forum post; notes missing depth-buffer details
Atmosphere shader conflicts with clouds; parachute simulation dropped for simple animation
Delivery UI picks random country and city; scoring by distance; presenter guesses Maseru, Madagascar
Reflects game is more fun to make than play; ideas: pirates, lighthouses, weather; asks viewers for ideas; Bogota miss

metrics.brute_force: yes 12:10: slow per-pixel loop over every country and segment, kept because it works, with a faster idea deferred
metrics.examples: ~12 independent features, each visualised once; no repeated examples; later features reuse earlier outputs (sphere mapping, compute shaders)
metrics.ending: Reflection on fun vs playability, list of ideas, Bogota geography miss; invites viewers to comment

principles.1: partly: opens with a familiar project story and a globe, but assumes shader/graphics literacy
principles.2: partly: terms like normalize, normal vector, frustum culling defined in one sentence on first use (1:07, 7:28, 8:26)
principles.3: not-observed: no habit-forming interface; Unity code shown briefly
principles.4: contradicted: little analogy; mostly direct technique plus visual result
principles.5: partly: tests at poles, flying the plane literally (6:14) but not framed as acting out
principles.6: confirmed: slow compute shaders accepted as first version (12:10, 17:19)
principles.7: partly: sea level slider (5:26) lets viewer see depth emerge; otherwise demonstration not discovery
principles.8: contradicted/not-observed: idea rate stays high; code shown briefly and skipped ('not terribly interesting')
principles.10: partly: cube to sphere to terrain to countries to gameplay is a progressive build
principles.11: confirmed: sphere before heightmap before normals before country data before highlighting
principles.12: confirmed: shuttle radar data, forum post, old videos, geology and Wikipedia detours
principles.13: partly: plain tone and honest limits, expert-level GPU depth, tool choice rarely justified

new_moves.name: deliberate-skip-with-pointer
new_moves.what: states what he is skipping and why, gives pointer for the curious ('in case you want to know')

new_moves.name: curiosity-detour
new_moves.what: digresses into geology facts triggered by what the visual shows, signals genuine interest

new_moves.name: visible-debugging
new_moves.what: shows the buggy output on screen before the fix

theory: This is a build log, not a lesson: trust comes from showing bugs, shortcuts, and uncertainty alongside the results, with each feature motivated by what the previous visual output lacked. Concepts are defined minimally exactly when the visual demands them.
velocity: Scene builder: a 'what is missing from the last output' prompt can sequence stacked builds
Voice: say what is being skipped and why, with pointer, rather than silently omitting detail
Orchestrator: allow short curiosity detours tied to the visual, capped, for rapport
Evals: this video is weak on repetition and analogy; do not use as the model for beginner pacing
Learner model: a slider on a single parameter (sea level) is a cheap discovery device
quote: sadly I don't know what it is
